item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is meaningfully closer to the frozen contract because it exposes the required Upload signature with opts ...FilesOption. Neither patch is merge-ready: both bypass FilesService.Add, add forbidden association-field machinery, refactor retry behavior, and omit source-reader-error coverage.","reasons":["B matches the exact required public API: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces UploadFileOption, so existing FilesOption values are not uniformly accepted.","B keeps the existing FilesOption interface and existing option constructors' return types intact. A adds two new option interfaces and changes WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions return types, creating unnecessary API churn.","Both correctly encode a replayable multipart body with field name \"file\" and validate empty filenames and nil content.","Both violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add, duplicating its request, header, decoding, and error path with direct Raw.Do calls instead. This weakens maintainability and semantic fidelity equally broadly in both patches but does not erase B's signature advantage."],"risks_a":["Directly contradicts the required Upload signature by accepting ...UploadFileOption.","Adds multiple typed association options and raw form-field support despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.","Changes public option return types and introduces duplicate option configuration machinery, risking compatibility and confusing the API model even if current gates pass type checks used by tests/examples in scope here are insufficient to prove broader source compatibility for function-typed uses or interface expectations outside the suite; more importantly, the frozen contract explicitly requires FilesOption behavior unchanged and A changes the public option model. Missing source-reader failure coverage also leaves required error propagation unverified. A additionally makes broad RawClient/retry, documentation, and RetryPolicy comment changes beyond the requested implementation path."],"risks_b":["WithFilesFormFields adds forbidden association-field functionality and stores it in shared filesOptions even though other methods ignore it.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, so future Add option, decoding, or error changes can diverge.","The broad enableBodyReplay change is outside contract scope; its SeekEnd probe can also leave unusual seekers at an uncertain position if SeekEnd fails after mutating state, because it only restores the starting offset on success. Source-reader failures are not tested, and the retry test checks multipart content only on the second attempt, weakening proof that the first streamed attempt carried the same body."]}
